Your digital product checkout is more than a payment button. 👀 If you sell ebooks, templates, courses, guides, Canva templates, or other digital products, you need to think about what happens after someone clicks “buy.” Before selling your first digital product, make sure you have: 1️⃣ Purchase terms — what the customer is actually agreeing to when they buy. 2️⃣ License & use restrictions — what they can and cannot do with your product. 3️⃣ Privacy Policy — especially if you’re collecting customer information. 4️⃣ Website/store terms — the rules governing purchases and use of your store. 5️⃣ Protection against unauthorized sharing & reselling — because your digital product should not become the internet’s free download. 😭 Your creativity is an asset. Treat it like one. And remember: your legal protection shouldn’t start after someone steals or misuses your digital product. It should be part of your business from the beginning. So… what exactly is a digital product? 👀 A digital product is something people can purchase and receive online—no physical inventory or shipping required. Think:  ✨ Ebooks ✨ Guides ✨ Templates ✨ Planners ✨ Checklists ✨ Workbooks ✨ Courses And here's something I didn't understand when I first started: You don't always have to create everything from scratch. There are several ways to get started: 🤎 Create your own — You create a product based on your knowledge, experience, or a problem you can help someone solve. 🤎 PLR (Private Label Rights) — You purchase a product with a license that may allow you to edit, rebrand, and sell it as your own, depending on the specific license terms. 🤎 MRR (Master Resell Rights) — You purchase a product that comes with rights that may allow you to resell it and, depending on the license, pass certain resale rights to your customers. 🤎 Affiliate Marketing — You don't own the product. You recommend someone else's product using your unique affiliate link and earn a commission when an eligible purchase is made. The key? 🔑 Don't just pick a random product because you can sell it. Start with WHO you want to help and WHAT problem they need solved. I'm learning this journey too, and I'm breaking it down in simple terms as I go.
